questions.question: Work out 48 times 5 by two different techniques and show that they agree.
questions.expected_answer: Breaking down: 40 times 5 is 200 and 8 times 5 is 40, total 240. Compensating: 50 times 5 is 250, minus 2 times 5 which is 10, gives 240. Or halving: 48 times 10 is 480, half is 240. All give 240.

questions.question: Explain why halving one number and doubling the other does not change the answer, using 16 times 25.
questions.expected_answer: 16 trays of 25 rolls can be pushed together in pairs to make 8 trays of 50 rolls. No rolls were added or removed, only regrouped, so 16 times 25 and 8 times 50 are both 400.

questions.question: Show how division checks that 15 times 12 equals 180.
questions.expected_answer: Division undoes multiplication, so 180 divided by 12 should give 15. Twelve times 10 is 120, leaving 60, and twelve times 5 is 60, so 180 divided by 12 is 15. The product is confirmed.
